subject.title: [Security] CSRF risk via dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback on network-exposed gateway (V-02)

question: Should OpenClaw keep, harden, or remove `gateway.controlUi.dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback` for exposed Gateway deployments?
rationale: The current branch is an intentional documented dangerous mode, and changing it affects both the Gateway browser security boundary and compatibility for operators who selected the escape hatch.

options.title: Harden the dangerous mode
options.body: Preserve the explicit flag for now, but add focused defenses such as `Sec-Fetch-Site` or CSRF-token checks plus tests for same-host/DNS-rebinding-style cases.

options.title: Remove with migration
options.body: Delete Host-header fallback and provide doctor/docs guidance that migrates users to explicit `allowedOrigins` or a safer approved alternative.

options.title: Accept current policy
options.body: Keep the dangerous operator-selected mode as-is and rely on critical audit findings plus deployment documentation.

recommendation.title: Harden the dangerous mode
recommendation.body: Preserve the explicit flag for now, but add focused defenses such as `Sec-Fetch-Site` or CSRF-token checks plus tests for same-host/DNS-rebinding-style cases.

likelyOwner.reason: CODEOWNERS explicitly routes the affected Gateway auth/security files and docs to this security review owner.
